newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends up, specs liquidate December.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends up, specs liquidate December.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended higher in brisk activity as speculators liquidated December contracts and rolled December contracts into March, floor sources said.
Dealers said trade will remain brisk but rangebound ahead of the first notice day for December contracts on November 22. Open interest remains high at 13,677 lots, down 3,510.
Resistance was pegged at Friday's high of 73.00 in December, where trade selling is likely to emerge. Support was seen at Friday's low of 71.50.
"We're locked in that range until we get into deliveries," one dealer said.
December closed up 0.79 at 72.29, having ranged from 72.85 to 71.85. March ended 0.65 higher at 74.07.
Talk of export business conducted over the weekend may have encouraged buying on the open, traders said, while attributing today's higher prices to mostly technical factors.
Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said Friday's close at 71.50, above the ten-day moving average of 71.45 basis December, was positive for prices.
A dearth of selling eased the move higher, she said.
